facts.rationale: Corrects collision-line versus joint terminology and the disabling operation while preserving supported configuration consumers without making a compiled layout claim.
facts.value: At source level, grSh_Route_StageData binds Gr_Kind_ShrineRoute and /GrNSr.dat to the lifecycle hooks and seven-entry stage_callbacks table. The object setup helper indexes that table by object ID. grSh_Route_803E58E0 supplies seven collision-line IDs to mpLib_800575B0, which disables each valid line and refreshes its owning joint's connectivity. light_config is applied to successive existing light nodes after the head, while lobj0 and lobj1 are loaded and appended as auxiliary diffuse and specular lights. These source relationships do not establish compiled section residency.

evidence.why: Array, callback records and stage descriptor.
Fifteen configurations and two auxiliary descriptors.

facts.rationale: The list contains collision-line exclusions, not map joints to restore; source declarations alone do not prove section placement.
facts.value: The source's initialized configuration comprises an eight-element collision-line exclusion array whose first seven entries are consumed, a seven-entry ground-object callback table, the Shrine Route stage descriptor, fifteen environmental-light configurations, and two descriptors for appended auxiliary diffuse and specular lights. Exact placement of these declarations in the compiled .data section remains unverified.

evidence.why: Ten point and five combined-type records and their interpretation.
Canonical point, spot and contribution masks.

facts.rationale: Independent type definitions establish that the combined low bits encode spot lights.
facts.value: The source callback table defines seven ground-object behavior classes. Entry 4 uniquely carries flags 0xC0000000; the stage descriptor enables bit 0 and has no GrJoint table. The light configuration contains ten type-2 point lights and five type-3 spot lights, all configured for diffuse contribution. LOBJ_FLAGS_B1 | LOBJ_INFINITE encodes LOBJ_SPOT rather than an infinite-light category. Two separate diffuse/specular descriptor-loaded lights are appended for runtime control. These observations describe source configuration, not compiled section layout.

evidence.why: Scalar references and initial light positions.
Strict X bounds and upper Y threshold only.

facts.rationale: Corrects the trigger geometry and avoids deriving either section layout or runtime descriptor-union semantics from source names.
facts.value: The associated source constants support two appended runtime lights and a scaled regional position test. The light constructors copy (0,100,0), and their descriptors reference two source scalars named lobj0_shininess and lobj1_shininess. The regional test uses an open X interval below a Y threshold, with no lower Y bound or Z test; it is not a bounded rectangle. Compiled .sdata residency and the descriptor loader's interpretation of the scalar pointers must be established separately.

evidence.why: Weighted direction and distinct selected-source color path.

facts.rationale: Separates actual directional blending from single-source RGB attenuation and preserves the compiled-evidence boundary.
facts.value: Source scalar literals parameterize camera interpolation, randomized angular acceleration, damping, rotation bounds and wrapping, and player-relative lighting. The lighting process ranks type-dependent distances and accumulates weighted directions; its specular color comes from sorted source index 1 and is attenuated according to the distance gap to sorted index 2. It does not blend multiple source colors. These source uses do not independently identify the literals' compiled .sdata2 placement.

facts.rationale: Preserves guarded marker setup and numeric transitions while removing an unsupported delayed-completion interpretation.
facts.value: Selects exactly one of six local flags at random. For each existing source joint, creates a class-3 marker at the selected slot or class-1 marker otherwise, stores the result, and configures translation and uniform scale only when the object and its JObj exist. Missing joints leave their slots unchanged. Later, an unfinished chamber with marker map_id 3 selects state 6 and assigns xD0 = 0x3C; state 6 sets stage flag 0x10 without testing or decrementing xD0. Thus the assignment does not establish a 60-frame completion delay. Other markers select encounter-preparation state 1.

evidence.why: Complete state, object, collision and camera data flow.
Transition argument stored as overlay command pointer.

facts.rationale: Corrects latch count and parameter interpretation and records the exceptional encounter-object lifetime branch.
facts.value: Reads player position/status, two shared contact latches xCA/xCC fed by six monitored joints, six retained marker pointers and their map IDs, Yakumono trigger/transition parameters, completion predicates and camera offset. Writes numeric controller state, selected chamber, completion mask, encounter-object reference xD4, interpolation timer xCE, stage flags, visibility, collision membership and three camera-relative JObj translations. It clears both contact latches at the end of the update. Transition fields passed to grMaterial_801C9604 become overlay command pointers in that callee, not established animation indices. State 4 admits xD4 == 0 in its completion condition but dereferences xD4->hsd_obj before the subsequent nonzero destruction guard; this path must not be described as null-safe cleanup.

evidence.why: Also invoked for the initial lighting update.

facts.rationale: The function is object 6's recurring gobj_proc as well as an immediate initialization call. Update expresses this persistent role better than Setup without changing the supported player-relative lighting interpretation.
Corrects light-type decoding using independent canonical definitions while preserving the configuration data flow.
facts.value: Starting after the light-list head, applies successive light_config records to existing HSD_LObj nodes. Each valid node receives color, position and distance attenuation. Type 2 records receive point-plus-diffuse flags; type 3 records receive spot-plus-diffuse flags and additionally receive interest and spotlight cutoff/function. The source spells type 3 as LOBJ_FLAGS_B1 | LOBJ_INFINITE, but the combined value is LOBJ_SPOT, not an infinite light. Missing nodes take the diagnostic branch.

evidence.why: Null guard, loop, type branches and diagnostic call.

facts.rationale: Corrects the infinite-light category and preserves the exact missing-node behavior, including the malformed diagnostic call.
facts.value: A null GObj is a no-op. Otherwise the function traverses all fifteen configuration records in lockstep with the light chain after its head, reconfiguring existing nodes without allocation. Type-2 point and type-3 spot records use separate flag branches; only the spot branch installs interest and cone parameters. A missing node invokes OSReport and subsequent iterations continue with null nodes because HSD_LObjGetNext(NULL) returns NULL. The diagnostic format contains %s and %d but this call supplies no corresponding arguments, so that error path should not be described as a well-formed report.

evidence.why: Direction and color consumers target different lights.

facts.rationale: Corrects attribution of nearby source colors to the wrong auxiliary light.
facts.value: Supports the Underground Maze's player-responsive lighting by creating the diffuse auxiliary retained in x16C. The lighting process positions and aims it using the player and a weighted combination of surrounding source-light directions. Nearby source-color copying and attenuation instead update the separate specular auxiliary in x170; they are not applied to this constructor's light by that process.

evidence.why: Object 4 and supporting objects created at startup.
Randomized six-chamber markers and monitored floors.
